decisions_taken_from_it_labelled_as_inte.mind: A Mind (^1) is an entity, a being, anything that thinks: a machine, a human, an animal, an AI, and so on. In labeling, every such being that a passage names is listed as a Mind. A label team no longer leaves a person out because the passage shows nothing of that person's awareness. The canonical definition line of ^1 is unchanged and is still quoted word for word; the owner's sentence is quoted beside it as the owner's ruling.
decisions_taken_from_it_labelled_as_inte.presence_of_positive_and_negative: Whether a thing is Positive (^2) or Negative (^3) for a Mind is decided with the canonical colloquialisms of Clarification 6, not with working lines written by the study's builders.
decisions_taken_from_it_labelled_as_inte.presence_of_the_other_noetics: The same holds for ^4 to ^9 (and ^1): the Colloquialism Test of Clarification 6 decides. Ask what saying a native speaker would use for the moment; mark the Noetic whose canonical sayings and definition it matches; if several match, mark each; if none matches, mark nothing.
decisions_taken_from_it_labelled_as_inte.what_stays: The ten definitions word for word. The anti-drift annotations of Clarification 6 (^3 is visceral, not analytical; ^8 is triggering, not reasoning). The Clarification 6 guardrail: where a colloquialism and a definition appear to disagree, the definition governs. The owner's working ruling on reading a sign (guide rule 15) until the owner answers the two questions below. The format rules on how a pair or a lone entry is written (guide rules 2 and 3 as they now stand): they do not decide presence.
decisions_taken_from_it_labelled_as_inte.what_goes: The study's own narrowing rules on presence from guide v1.2 (for example: ^4 needs words for how much; a length of time alone is ^5 and not ^7; who is and is not listed as a Mind), including 'mark neither when only one of the pair is given' (rule 2) and 'recall on purpose is not a pair' (rule 3), and every 'held kind' and 'working line' of the rejected v2.0. The full canonical map of sayings replaces the shortened table in the guide's Part A.
